verifications.claim: An immaculate inning in baseball occurs when a pitcher strikes out all three batters in a single inning using exactly nine pitches.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: '9 PITCHES – 9 STRIKES – SIDE RETIRED: IMMACULATE INNINGS'; R3: 'An immaculate inning is when a pitcher strikes out three batters, on three strikes each. ... Nine pitches total.'; R5: 'An immaculate inning occurs when a pitcher strikes out all three batters he faces in one inning, using the minimum possible number of pitches - nine.'; R6: 'An immaculate inning occurs in baseball when a pitcher strikes out all three batters he faces in one inning using the minimum possible number of pitches: nine.'; R7: 'Three up, three down, with all three batters struck out on three pitches each.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly define immaculate inning as three strikeouts on exactly nine pitches.
